doc_description: Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2017 (filed February 1, 2018) detailing its North America, International, and AWS segments, the consolidation of Whole Foods Market beginning August 28, 2017, extensive risk and market disclosures, and audited results showing $177.9B in net sales and $3.0B in net income for Nasdaq-listed AMZN.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
- SEC Form 10-K for Amazon.com, Inc. for fiscal year ended December 31, 2017; Nasdaq-listed (AMZN); incorporated in Delaware; HQ in Seattle; well-known seasoned issuer; large accelerated filer; not a shell; in compliance with filing and XBRL requirements.
- Cover-page metrics: aggregate market value of non-affiliate voting stock as of June 30, 2017 of ~$387.3B; 484,107,183 shares outstanding as of January 24, 2018.
- Documents incorporated by reference: portions of the 2018 definitive proxy statement for Part III items.
- Table of contents outlines standard 10-K sections across Parts I–IV, including Business, Risk Factors, Properties, Legal Proceedings, MD&A, Financial Statements, Controls and Procedures, and others.
- Item 1 Business highlights:
  - Forward-looking statements caution.
  - Company background: founded 1994, IPO in 1997; mission to be Earth’s most customer-centric company; guiding principles include customer obsession, invention, operational excellence, long-term thinking.
  - Operating segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS); Whole Foods Market results consolidated from August 28, 2017.
  - Customer sets and offerings:
    - Consumers: retail websites and physical stores; access via websites, mobile apps, Alexa, and stores; devices (Kindle, Fire tablets, Fire TV, Echo); media content; Amazon Prime (free shipping, video streaming, and other benefits); multiple fulfillment methods (owned networks, co-sourced/outsourced, digital delivery); global customer service.
    - Sellers: marketplace and fulfillment programs enabling third parties to sell on Amazon or their own sites; Amazon not seller of record; revenue from fixed/variable fees, per-unit fees, and interest.
    - Developers and enterprises: AWS provides global compute, storage, database, and other cloud services to startups, enterprises, government, and academia.
  - Additional services: advertising and co-branded credit card agreements.
  - R&D reported within “Technology and content”; segment information referenced to financial statement notes.

structure.summary:
The excerpt is from Amazon.com, Inc.’s Annual Report (Form 10-K), Part I, Item 1: Business. It includes:
- Forward-looking statements caution and reference to Risk Factors (Item 1A).
- Corporate background: incorporation (1994 WA; 1996 DE), headquarters (Seattle), IPO (1997), Nasdaq listing (AMZN).
- Mission and operating principles: customer obsession, invention, operational excellence, long-term thinking.
- Business organization into three segments—North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS)—used for performance evaluation and operations management; references to segment note and R&D presentation in financial statements.
- Inclusion of Whole Foods Market results since its August 28, 2017 acquisition.
- Consumers: retail websites and physical stores; vast product selection from Amazon and third parties; access via web, mobile apps, Alexa, and stores; Amazon devices (Kindle, Fire tablets, Fire TV, Echo) and media content; low-price focus; Amazon Prime benefits (free shipping, streaming, others); fulfillment via Amazon-operated networks, co-sourced/outsourced logistics, digital delivery, and stores; global customer service network.
- Sellers: programs enabling third parties to sell on Amazon sites and their own sites, with Amazon not the seller of record; revenue from various seller fees and interest.
- Developers and enterprises: AWS offering broad global compute, storage, database, and related services to customers including startups, government agencies, and academic institutions.
- Mention of additional services such as advertising and co-branded credit card arrangements.

structure.heading: Item 1. Business
structure.start_phrase:
This Annual Report on Form 10-K and the documents incorporated here
in by reference contain forward-looking statements based on expectations,estimates, and projections as of the da
te of this filing.
structure.summary:
- Overview of Amazon.com, Inc. as presented in its Annual Report on Form 10-K: corporate history (1994 founding, 1997 IPO), Delaware incorporation, Seattle headquarters, Nasdaq ticker AMZN, and mission guided by customer obsession, invention, operational excellence, and long-term thinking.
- Business organization into three reportable segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS); inclusion of Whole Foods Market results from August 28, 2017.
- Consumer-facing operations: extensive selection across categories via websites, mobile apps, Alexa, and physical stores; own devices (Kindle, Fire tablets/TV, Echo) and media production; Amazon Prime benefits; multi-channel fulfillment (owned networks, co-/outsourced, digital delivery, stores) and global customer service.
- Seller services: marketplace programs enabling third-party sales on Amazon and sellers’ own sites; fee structures and fulfillment options where Amazon is not seller of record.
- Developer and enterprise services: AWS offerings spanning global compute, storage, database, and related services for organizations of all sizes, including public sector and academia.
- Content creator programs: Kindle Direct Publishing with 70% royalty option, Amazon Publishing, and platforms for creators of books, music, film, apps, and other content.
- Competitive landscape: intense, rapidly evolving competition across retail (online/offline/multichannel), media, search/comparison/social discovery, e-commerce enablement, logistics/fulfillment, IT/cloud, and consumer electronics; key competitive factors include selection, price, convenience, fulfillment speed/reliability, service quality, and customer switching frictions; recognition of competitors’ resource advantages and potential for new entrants and business models.
- Intellectual property: reliance on trademarks, copyrights, patents, domain names, trade secrets, and licensing to protect and leverage proprietary technologies, with U.S. and international registrations and filings.
- Seasonality: concentration of revenue in Q4 (33% in 2015, 32% in 2016, 34% in 2017), with 2017 Q4 including Whole Foods contribution.
- Workforce: approximately 566,000 employees as of December 31, 2017; use of contractors/temporary staff; presence of works councils/unions in certain regions; strong competition for technical talent.
- Investor information: availability of SEC filings, governance materials, press releases, and select social media on the investor relations website (www.amazon.com/ir).
- Leadership: listing of executive officers (e.g., Jeffrey P. Bezos as President/CEO/Chair; Andrew Jassy as CEO AWS; Brian Olsavsky as CFO) and Board of Directors as of January 24, 2018, with brief role histories.
- Key risk factors highlighted:
  - Intense competition across all business lines and geographies, including from larger and better-resourced rivals and new technologies.
  - Strain from rapid global expansion and scaling of offerings and infrastructure on management, operations, systems, and financial controls.
  - Additional risks from entering new products, services, technologies, and regions, including adoption uncertainty, technology challenges, service quality exposure, and potentially lower profitability.
  - Potential for significant fluctuations in operating results and growth rates due to demand variability, macroeconomic conditions, fixed-cost structures, and factors such as customer retention/acquisition, seller network expansion, inventory and fulfillment effectiveness, competitive actions, technology/internet adoption trends, and timing/costs of system and infrastructure expansions.

structure.title: Risk Factors
structure.heading: Item 1A. Risk Factors
structure.start_phrase:
Please carefully consid
er the following risk factors.
structure.summary:
- This excerpt is the Risk Factors section (Item 1A) of a large global e-commerce and cloud services company’s annual report, detailing material risks that could adversely affect business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows.
- Competitive landscape: Intense, rapidly evolving competition across retail, e-commerce services, digital content, electronic devices, and web/infrastructure computing; rivals may have greater resources, better vendor terms, aggressive pricing, and new technologies/business models.
- Operational scale and growth: Rapid global expansion strains management, personnel, systems, infrastructure, finances, and internal controls; risks from entering new products, services, technologies, and geographies with uncertain adoption and profitability.
- Financial variability: Significant fluctuations in revenue, operating results, and growth rates due to forecasting challenges, demand changes, customer and seller retention, pricing, internet adoption, system expansion costs, legal outcomes, product/service mix, returns, shipping offers, investment levels, fuel/commodity prices, partner performance, network access fees, collections, security incidents, and geopolitical events.
- International risks: High costs and uncertain profitability abroad; exposure to local economic/political conditions, e-commerce/device regulation, trade barriers, IP enforcement variability, licensing, currency controls, infrastructure limitations, working-capital cycles, consumer/data protection rules, lower internet/credit usage, staffing/cultural issues, labor laws, anti-corruption compliance, trade/tax policy shifts, war/terrorism, and strong local competitors.
- China and India regulatory structures: Ownership and licensing constraints require local structures and partnerships; legal uncertainty could lead to fines, license revocations, or shutdowns; funding and contract enforceability risks.
- Fulfillment and data centers: Demand forecasting and network optimization challenges; capacity mismatches, higher costs, impairments; staffing constraints; dependence on a limited number of carriers; vulnerability to weather, disasters, labor disputes, and similar disruptions; complexities from holding third-party inventory.
- Seasonality: Fourth-quarter concentration increases risks of stock-outs or overstocking, higher shipping costs, site performance issues, and staffing shortfalls; year-end cash and payables seasonality.
- Commercial agreements/alliances: Complex, resource-intensive arrangements with variable compensation and renewal risk; potential integration difficulties and third-party claims.
- Acquisitions and investments: Integration, retention, losses/expenses, asset and goodwill impairments, reliance on investee controls, implementing public-company controls, unknown liabilities, cross-border complexities; potential dilution, debt, and valuation impairments.
- Foreign exchange: Translation and remeasurement volatility; exposure from holding non-USD cash and securities.
- Key personnel: Dependence on senior leadership, notably the CEO; no key-person insurance.
- Data security/privacy: Risks of data loss or breaches (including vendor systems); prior incidents; controls can’t provide absolute security.
- System reliability: Website/service interruptions from capacity constraints, disasters, cyber events, or insufficient redundancy; potentially inadequate insurance.
- Inventory risk: Seasonality, rapid product cycles/pricing shifts, defects, changing demand/tastes, spoilage, long lead times and prepayments, and high consumer electronics exposure.
- Intellectual property: Limits of protection and domain control globally; costs and challenges enforcing rights; exposure to infringement claims and “patent assertion entities”; DRM vulnerabilities for digital content.
- Business model and stock volatility: Rapidly evolving model with highly volatile stock price influenced by rates, sector trends, quarterly results, analyst actions, capital structure changes, peer valuations, and investor activity; implications for compensation and dilution.
- Government regulation: Expanding and evolving laws on taxation, privacy/data protection, pricing, content/copyrights, distribution/transportation, mobile/electronic devices, e-waste/energy, environment, contracting/communications, competition, consumer protection, employment, trade/protectionism, web services, payments, net neutrality/access, drones, health/sanitation, labeling, and marketplace seller rules.
- Sales/indirect taxes: Growing obligations for remote sellers/marketplaces to collect transaction taxes; compliance system challenges, potential retroactive liabilities, penalties; expanding information reporting mandates; possible shifts in U.S. precedent.
- Income taxes: Exposure to changing tax laws and judgments (including U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017), audits, and litigation; IRS transfer pricing dispute on appeal; EU state aid matter in Luxembourg; potential for additional liabilities and volatility in effective tax rate.
- Supplier dependencies: Reliance on key/limited suppliers and licensors; risks from bankruptcies, delays, disruptions, and unethical or noncompliant practices affecting reputation and results.
- Government contracts: Subject to procurement rules, audits, investigations, penalties, and termination for convenience.
- Product liability/food safety: Exposure to claims, recalls, insurance limitations; added risk from third-party sellers.
- Payments risks: Regulatory and compliance burdens (including enhanced authentication), fraud, rising interchange/fees, reliance on processors and co-branded programs, card network rules and data security; money transmission/AML, privacy, and funds-handling obligations.
- Marketplace liability: Potential liability and reimbursement costs for fraudulent or unlawful seller activities under buyer protection guarantees.
- Item 1B (Unresolved Staff Comments): None.

structure.start_phrase:
The following selected consol
idated financial data should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and the notes thereto in Item 8 ofPart II, “Financial Stat
ements and Supplementary Data,” and the information contained in Item 7 of Part II, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of FinancialCondition and Results of Operations.”
structure.summary:
- Item 6 — Selected Consolidated Financial Data (2013–2017):
  - Five-year summary of key metrics (in millions, except per share data): net sales, operating income, net income (loss), basic and diluted EPS, weighted-average shares, and net cash provided by operating activities.
  - Trend highlights: net sales grew from $74.5B (2013) to $177.9B (2017); operating income rose from $0.7B to over $4.1B; net income moved from a loss in 2014 to $3.0B in 2017; operating cash flow increased from $5.6B to $18.4B; total assets expanded to $131.3B and long-term obligations to $45.7B by 2017.
  - Notes:
    - Whole Foods Market acquisition (Aug 28, 2017); results included from acquisition date.
    - EPS details referenced to Note 1 in the financial statements.
    - Cash flow reclassification: retrospective adjustment moving excess tax benefits from financing to operating activities due to new accounting guidance.

- Item 7 — Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A):
  - Forward-Looking Statements:
    - Safe-harbor caution regarding statements about guidance, industry prospects, and future operating/financial results.
    - Key uncertainties cited: FX fluctuations, global economic conditions and spending, internet/online commerce/cloud growth rates, timing and magnitude of investments, sales mix (products vs. services), tax exposure, competition, growth management, operating variability, international expansion, legal outcomes, fulfillment/sortation/delivery/data center optimization, inventory risks, seasonality, commercial agreements, M&A/strategic transactions, payments risk, throughput/productivity, and amplified macroeconomic risks; cross-referenced to Risk Factors.
  - Business Overview and Revenue Model:
    - Primary revenue from selling a wide range of products and services via consumer websites and physical stores.
    - Offerings include first-party merchandise/content, third-party marketplace sales, and company-manufactured electronic devices.
    - Revenue recognition: gross for items sold from inventory (product sales); net share for third-party seller items (service sales).
    - Additional services: AWS (compute, storage, database), fulfillment, publishing, digital content subscriptions, advertising, co-branded credit cards.
    - Strategy to increase unit sales through broader selection, more categories, and enhanced customer experience (lower prices, availability, faster delivery/performance, richer product info, ease of use, reliability, and trust).
  - Financial Focus and Cost Structure:
    - Emphasis on long-term, sustainable growth in free cash flows (non-GAAP), driven by operating income growth, working capital management, and cash capital expenditures (including buy vs. lease decisions).
    - Operating income growth targeted via higher sales and efficient cost management, while investing in long-term initiatives.
    - Variable costs: product/content, payment processing and transaction costs, picking/packing/shipping, transportation, customer service, AWS operating costs, and a portion of marketing.
    - Fixed costs: technology infrastructure; development and enhancement of websites, web services, devices, and digital offerings; fulfillment centers and physical stores.
    - Cost-reduction initiatives: increase direct sourcing, secure greater supplier discounts, reduce process defects, improve efficiencies, and maintain a lean culture.
    - Working capital defined as accounts receivable, inventory, and accounts payable; free cash flow and related non-GAAP measures referenced for further detail.

structure.title: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.heading: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase:
This Annual Report on Form 10-K includes forward
-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995.
structure.summary:
- Cautionary forward-looking statements outlining uncertainties affecting results, including FX, economic conditions, competition, logistics, technology spending, taxes, and legal outcomes.
- Business overview: revenue streams from product sales, third-party marketplace services, devices, subscriptions, advertising, co-branded credit cards, and AWS; recognition of gross vs net revenue; emphasis on broad selection and customer experience.
- Long-term financial focus on sustainable free cash flow through operating income growth, efficient working capital and capital spending; discussion of variable vs fixed costs, inventory velocity and cash-generating operating cycle; FX translation impacts on results.
- Investment priorities: technology and content (including AWS, devices, infrastructure, new categories/geographies); approach to managing shareholder dilution with RSUs.
- Critical accounting judgments: inventory valuation and sensitivity; supplier commitments; complex income tax considerations including impacts of the 2017 U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, IRS transfer pricing dispute and appeal, and EU state aid/Luxembourg matter; potential for material changes from audits and evolving guidance.
- Liquidity and capital resources: cash flow trends (2015–2017) for operating, investing, and financing activities; cash and marketable securities balances and FX composition; capital expenditures and capital/finance leases (notably for AWS infrastructure); Whole Foods Market acquisition financing via $16B senior notes; credit facilities status; tax benefits, cash taxes, NOLs and credits; restricted cash; purchase obligations; expectation of sufficient liquidity and potential future financing actions.
- Results of operations by segment (North America, International, AWS): net sales growth (with FX effects), segment mix, and drivers (unit growth, pricing, selection, Whole Foods impact); operating income—North America growth, larger International losses, strong AWS profitability; detailed operating expense trends (cost of sales, fulfillment, marketing, technology and content, G&A, other), including rising shipping and fulfillment costs and ongoing tech/content investment.
- Interest and other income/expense: higher interest income with larger balances, rising interest expense with more leases/debt, other income driven by FX and equity warrant valuation; long-term debt and other long-term liabilities levels.
- Income taxes: provisional 2017 Tax Act benefit, effective tax rate drivers, valuation allowance in Luxembourg, available U.S. tax credits and NOLs, and expectations for future cash taxes.
- Equity-method investment losses and impairments.
- Non-GAAP measures: definitions and reconciliations for free cash flow and variants (less lease principal repayments; less finance lease principal and assets acquired under capital leases), with noted limitations.
- Constant-currency analysis showing effects of foreign exchange rates on net sales, operating expenses, and operating income.
- Q1 2018 guidance: projected net sales growth range (with FX tailwind), operating income range, and assumption of no additional major transactions.
- Market risk disclosures: sensitivity to interest rate changes (investment portfolio fair values) and FX fluctuations; maturity profile and weighted-average yields of cash equivalents and marketable securities.

structure.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.heading: Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.start_phrase:
We are exposed to market ri
sk for the effect of interest rate changes, foreign currency fluctuations, and changes in the market values of our investments.
structure.summary:
- Section covered: Item 7A — Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk, with a subsequent index to Item 8 financial statements.

- Interest rate risk:
  - Exposure arises from the investment portfolio and fixed‑rate long‑term debt.
  - Debt is carried at amortized cost; fair value fluctuates with market rates but does not affect earnings unless retired.
  - Cash equivalents and marketable fixed‑income securities are available‑for‑sale and reported at fair value; portfolio focused on investment‑grade short‑ to intermediate‑term securities and AAA money market funds.
  - As of December 31, 2017, cash equivalents and marketable fixed‑income securities totaled about $22.3 billion across money market funds, corporate debt, U.S. government and agency securities, asset‑backed securities, foreign government and agency securities, and other securities, with weighted‑average yields generally between ~0.6% and ~2.6% depending on category and maturity.

- Long‑term debt profile:
  - Total debt of $24.9 billion (fixed‑rate unsecured notes) outstanding as of December 31, 2017, with maturities from 2019 to 2057 and coupons ranging from 1.90% to 5.20%.
  - Notable tranches include $3.5 billion due 2027 (3.15%), $3.5 billion due 2047 (4.05%), and $2.25 billion due 2057 (4.25%).
  - Fair value of total debt estimated at $26.4 billion (Level 2 inputs).

- Foreign exchange risk:
  - International segment contributed 30% of 2017 consolidated revenues; key operating currencies include the Euro, Japanese Yen, and British Pound.
  - FX movements affect reported sales, expenses, and intercompany balances; 2017 FX changes increased International net sales by $137 million versus prior year.
  - Foreign‑denominated cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities were $11.1 billion; assumed adverse FX shifts of 5%, 10%, and 20% would reduce fair value by approximately $555 million, $1.1 billion, and $2.2 billion, respectively (recorded in accumulated other comprehensive loss).
  - Intercompany balances are also exposed; 5%, 10%, and 20% adverse FX changes would result in losses of approximately $280 million, $600 million, and $1.3 billion, respectively (recorded in Other income (expense), net).

- Investment risk:
  - Equity and equity warrant investments totaled $737 million as of December 31, 2017.
  - Publicly traded portion of $415 million is measured at fair value and subject to market volatility.
  - Private investments are reviewed for other‑than‑temporary impairment based on operating trends, market transactions, and available data; market sensitivity analyses are not practicable due to valuation complexities.

- Cross‑references:
  - Additional detail is referenced to Item 7 MD&A sections on Liquidity and Capital Resources and the Effect of Foreign Exchange Rates.

- Financial statements index (Item 8):
  - Auditor’s report, consolidated statements of cash flows, operations, comprehensive income, balance sheets, stockholders’ equity, and notes, spanning pages 36–42.

structure.title: Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
structure.heading: Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data
structure.start_phrase:
We have audited the ac
companying consolidated balance sheets of Amazon.com, Inc. as of December 31, 2017 and 2016 , and the related consolid atedstatements of operat
ions, comprehensive income, stockholders’ equity, and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended December 31, 2017 and the related notes (collectively referred t
o as the ‘financial statements’).
structure.summary:
- Independent auditor’s report: Ernst & Young LLP issued unqualified opinions on Amazon’s 2017 and 2016 consolidated financial statements and on internal control over financial reporting.
- Consolidated financial statements presented: Statements of Cash Flows, Operations, Comprehensive Income, Balance Sheets, and Stockholders’ Equity for 2015–2017, with accompanying notes.
- Key results and trends (2015–2017):
  - Net sales grew to $177.9B in 2017; operating income $4.1B; net income $3.0B.
  - Operating cash flow $18.4B; significant investing outflows from capex and acquisitions; 2017 financing inflows from new debt.
  - Segment performance: North America and AWS generated operating income; International reported operating losses. AWS continued strong growth and profitability.
  - Revenue mix detailed: online stores, new physical stores line (Whole Foods), third‑party seller services, subscription services (Prime and digital), AWS, and advertising/other.
- Major acquisitions and balance sheet impacts:
  - 2017 acquisitions of Whole Foods Market (~$13.2B net of cash) and Souq (~$0.6B) plus smaller tech acquisitions.
  - Purchase price allocations, sizable goodwill increase to $13.35B; acquired intangible assets (notably Whole Foods trade name) and related amortization schedules.
  - Pro forma financial information for 2016/2017 reflecting acquisitions.
- Property, equipment, and leases:
  - Large growth in property and equipment (including servers, data centers, fulfillment, and buildings); extensive use of capital and finance leases and build‑to‑suit arrangements.
  - Detailed depreciation, segment asset allocations, and future lease obligations.
- Capital structure and liquidity:
  - Significant 2017 senior notes issuance (including to finance Whole Foods) raising total long‑term debt to ~$24.9B face value; details of maturities and interest rates.
  - Revolving credit facilities (secured seller‑receivables facility and unsecured $3.0B facility).
  - Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities composition, fair value hierarchy, maturities, and restricted balances.
- Accounting policies and estimates:
  - Revenue recognition for products, services, multiple‑element arrangements, Prime memberships; gross vs. net presentation; returns and incentives.
  - Cost classifications: cost of sales, fulfillment, marketing, technology and content, G&A.
  - Stock‑based compensation methodology and expense recognition; RSU activity and unrecognized cost.
  - Fair value measurement framework; inventories (lower of cost and NRV); internal‑use software capitalization; video and music content capitalization/amortization; investments; long‑lived asset impairment; unearned revenue (Prime and AWS).
  - Foreign currency translation and transaction gains/losses.
- Standards adoption and upcoming changes:
  - Recently adopted: inventory measurement update; stock‑based compensation tax effects reclassification to operating cash flows.
  - Not yet adopted: ASC 606 revenue standard (expected retained earnings increase primarily from gift cards and Prime classification), financial instruments update, ASC 842 leases (material balance sheet impact expected), and income tax guidance for intercompany asset transfers; restricted cash presentation.
- Income taxes:
  - 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act provisional benefit (~$789M) mainly from remeasurement of deferred taxes; discussion of mandatory tax on foreign earnings and intent to keep earnings invested abroad.
  - Tax provision components, U.S. vs. international pre‑tax income, deferred tax assets/liabilities, valuation allowances (notably Luxembourg), NOLs and credits.
  - Tax contingencies: IRS transfer pricing litigation (Tax Court favorable decision under appeal), French tax settlement, EU state aid decision involving Luxembourg (appealed; potential escrow funding).
- Commitments and contingencies:
  - Future commitments for debt service, capital/finance leases, operating leases, purchase obligations (including content and Whole Foods products), and build‑to‑suit projects.
  - Pledged assets for leases, payables to third‑party sellers, and credit facilities.
  - Other contingencies: U.S. sanctions/export control self‑reporting; sales tax assessment in South Carolina for third‑party seller transactions (disputed).
- Legal proceedings:
  - Overview of ongoing litigation including copyright levies in EU, wage and hour cases, and multiple patent cases related to AWS and digital services; company intends vigorous defense.
- Stockholders’ equity and AOCI:
  - Changes in additional paid‑in capital, retained earnings, and AOCI (foreign currency translation and available‑for‑sale securities).
  - No share repurchases; RSU grants, vesting schedules, stock‑based compensation expense by function, and remaining unrecognized compensation cost.
- Segment and geographic information:
  - Net sales and operating income by North America, International, and AWS; sales by product/service category; sales by major countries; segment assets and property & equipment by segment; depreciation by segment.
- Quarterly results (unaudited):
  - 2016 and 2017 quarterly net sales, operating income, EPS; seasonality noted and inclusion of Whole Foods from August 28, 2017.
- Controls and procedures:
  - Management concluded disclosure controls and internal control over financial reporting were effective as of December 31, 2017; no material changes in internal control during Q4 2017.
